brief: A free, plain-language guide to the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria. Ask a question in your own words and get the exact section, explained the way a knowledgeable friend would. It must feel friendly, proudly Nigerian and precise, and never like an official government seal.
criteria: Success: reads at 16 px in a browser tab, works in one colour, avoids the category's scales, gavels, pillars and coat-of-arms imagery, and stays clearly independent of government branding.

concepts.name: Open Book
concepts.idea: The Constitution as an open book that talks back: its green pages and white gutter echo the flag, and the gap above the gutter forms the Niger–Benue Y.
rationale: Says what the product does in one glance: read the law, and ask it questions
Green–white–green without drawing a flag; the confluence Y rewards a second look
Custom lowercase wordmark: round, open letters with hooked t's, so it reads warm rather than official
A dedicated small-size cut keeps the gutter and tail visible at 16 px

recommendation: Open Book is approved as the constitution.ng identity: green symbol with an ink wordmark, a light-green reversed version for dark screens, and a simplified cut for favicons.
next_steps: Swap the app's Àṣẹ mark, favicon and page title for constitution.ng
Run a trademark search before public launch
Proof the green on press before printing anything
